Subtitles.Static: The Savior of my soul!
Welcome back, Trent. The usual?
No... you know what, gimme the good stuff.
Celebrating something special?
Yeah. Two somethings. First up, I present the new improved debt-free Trent 2.0!
Ah, life after debt. Lazarus, this one's on me.
Thanks, bud. Everytime I hear you say that I suddenly remember who my favouritest person in the whole wide world is...
Yeah yeah. So if there's a 'first up', there's gotta be a 'second up'. Spit it out already before I die of curiosity.
Don't you die on me. Wouldn't know where to get free drinks.
So anyway, an old friend sent me this pad-message.
Check it out.

>Greetings, loser! This is Alaric, your old buddy and life coach. Great news - I've found a gig that'll patch that black hole in your wallet. Meet me on Magdeburg, Sigma-13 System ASAP! And I mean now, like yesterday, Trent!
Whatcha reckon?
I think you're the luckiest son of a bitch this side of the planet.
Naturally... but I mean... should I just up and go?

Well let's see. You could stay here and hang with your only real friend in the universe, eke out a miserable living, freeze your ass off in that dingy little flat of yours and die an alcoholic washed-up loser decades from now. Or you could grab life by the horns and fly off to live a real life... but don't let me influence you unduly.
If you feel so strongly about leaving here why haven't you flown the coop?

Well, see... this may be a shit hole, but it's my shit hole. My bar, my life... guess I've grown attached. And unlike you I don't have friends with get-rich-quick schemes offering to share the spoils. 'Sides if I leave, who'd save everyone's souls after a shitty day?
You're right, without you this place just wouldn't be the same. I guess I'll be heading out to spaceport, then. Take care.
Yeah go on, abandon me here. Good riddance to bad rubbish, don't let the door hit your ass on the way out... and Trent... good luck.
Ticket and travel documents, please.
Trent?.. You're not The Tr...
No, no I'm not.
So tired of being reminded that Edison Trent saved the universe, while Addison Trent saved pennies.
Hey Trent, you slowpoke you sure took your sweet time!
Good to see you too, Alaric. I came as fast as I could.
Yeah, you walk here or what? Anyway I heard you finally levelled up and beat your debt demon. Congrats. No debts, no strings, no lady... am I right?
Mhm, no ship nor spare cash either. But silver lining, - no headaches over filling other people's cargo holds, and what's mine is truly mine... all of this... lovely nothing.
A blank slate... great starting point to open a new chapter in your life, no?
Witty banter aside, I've found this crazy paying job, but I can't do it alone. I need a good pilot I can trust...

I'll provide you a ship of course. For my best friend, state of the art, all the bells and whistles.. bristling with weapons. From the last century. Maybe survive liftoff without exploding... or imploding... you never know. Classic Alaric, always a paragon of generosity.
All we have to do is escort some flush Rheinlanders from New Berlin to Bismark. Deep pockets, real generous paycheck, Kaching.
Hmm... what's the catch? Why would Rheinlanders fork out for hired guns to escort them within their own territory? Why not go to their own authorities...
Ah, I'm probably overthinking things. As they say, don't look a gift horse in the ass... And a genuine antique ship! I'm touched. You're really twisting my arm, Al!

I knew you'd see it my way. Your ship's awaiting you in the hangar. Best check it over, put some duct tape on the holes if you know what I mean... I'll meet you topside when you're ready to blow... I mean roll.
Guten tag, gentlemen. This is Trent, the friend and ace pilot I told you about previously.

Most excellent. We are so glad to see you. We have been having a few, how do you say, problems with puppies... nein, I mean pirates in our system. We hope they did not inconvenience you too much on your journey here.
Just a teeny bit. I'm glad we made it here in one piece.
Fanstastisch. If alles is gut, then let us depart immediately.
Vielen Dank for the most excellent escort! We have transferred the money into your account!
You're most welcome. Please feel free to contact us again if you need to.
As a.. how do you say... bogus? Sweetener of the deal? We have added you to our Hanseatic trading community freelancers' whitelist.
From now on, you may take on missions offered by Hanseatic merchants, mein friend.

Ah, thank you so much for your kind generosity, gentlemen! Trent, you hear that? We have been elevated from bottom feeding gutter trash to honest to God accredited freelancers of the Hanseatic trading community!
I'm overwhelmed...

And Herr Trent, a friendly word of advice: that ship of yours... it is more holey than the church and leakier than a faucet. If it wasn't so ugly you might be able to sell it to a museum. Perhaps best to change to something less likely to kill you.
Yeah... I'll think about it.
So, Trent, how're you adjusting to the heady life of a debt free freelancer?
It's exciting I'll give you that. Now that I have my very own ship, I'm ready to fly down the maw of the devil himself.

Ah, perhaps patch it up with some newer parts before that. I'm sure they still sell them in novelty stores... Or maybe just buy a new ship. Luts had a point. I'm sorry, I just couldn't afford get better than that pile of junk at short notice.

Yeah, well it's my pile of junk now. He can stick it where the sun don't shine. Not everyone is born a millionaire with a silver spoon stuck up his butt like him. Must be nice to have money to change ships as often as he changes women. Or men.
Well, cheapskate, then at least upgrade the guns. Those peashooters are just pathetic.

During the battle in that asteroid field, your generator looked like it was going to melt down trying to keep up with the guns. It certainly wouldn't hurt you to shell out for a better power generator. And take a close look at the rest of the package. The chassis, while classic, is very flexible and accomodates a lot of upgrades. Most of its modules can be replaced with... more modern ones...
OK Trent, I better get going. Got to attend to business and scout out our next job. Will you be okay here without me?
Yes mummy. I'll try to look after myself. Get going, asshole.
Tch, such language. See you soon!
Are you Wilhelm?
Herr Trent. We are pleased you have agreed to work with us.

Whoa now, let's not jump the gun. I can't say I'm not curious, but it's a little intimidating getting instructions on my Pad to report to a Rhineland battleship in the middle of nowhere. It's a little off-putting.
Perhaps you are mistaken, Herr Trent. We would never resort to such unrefined tactics, as gentlemen of the Rhineland empire. Could you have imagined these... supposed messages?
No, I'm dead certain. Look, they're right... here... what's going on? How did they disapp...

Unimportant. That you are here now tells us you are agreeable. Herr Trent, let's cut to the chase. But before this, I hope you understand, regardless of how our conversation ends, all details must remain strictly confidential.
Okay, my lips are sealed. You military types don't mess around... Give me the details. By the way, why me?
You proved yourself earlier at Brandenburg. We couldn't help but notice how you managed to stay alive and even score kills in that death trap poop bucket you are flying.
Again with the insults to my poor ship. She's a classic, okay? Let's get on to the mission, OK?
Alright. Like all governments, we have informants in the territories of our, shall we say, rivals. You are following?
Sure. Spies.

Informants. Not long ago, one of our sp... informants contacted us via a secure channel, reporting that he had critical information to disclose and that he was headed to our secured data transmission point. Predictably, he never arrived. We have had no word since, in the following week. It can only mean one thing - he is dead.

Based on analysis of chatter between station dispatchers and operators of emergency services in the area of interest, we have established that our informant was attacked and killed in his ship. There is an over 99% probability of this.
My condolences for your loss. How do I come into the picture?
We need you to find his ship and extricate the supposely critical data for us. Time is critical as activity of so-called "Junkers" in the area is escalating rapidly. You must get there ahead of them.
How am I supposed to do that? I'm a stranger here, and I'm all by my lonesome.

You will have help. We are aware of a certain eccentric technophile who's been tapping into their radio comms and tracking them. We've been keeping a close eye on him for a while now, hoping to recruit him.
Like me, eh? You going to send him an invitatory pad-Psalm too? Perhaps a firebomb?

No, Herr Kent, we are sending you to him. He has the most thorough intel regarding every event that's occurred in that region of space. You must find and recruit him, use him to locate the coordinates of the shipwreck, extricate the data and transfer it to us... Without letting any Junker or other scavengers beat you to it. Easy.
Oh that's all there is to it? Why didn't you say so. Walk in the park. When do I start.
There's no "I" in "TEAM". I'll be your assigned team-mate for this mission.
Oh so you're the "A"? Will you be the boss of me?

Nein. I will be your wingman and liason to the authorities - I have a fairly high standing and security clearance in Rheinland. The strategic and tactical aspects of this operation are entirely yours, Herr Trent. So if we fail, it's entirely on you. You understand my meaning, yes?
Ominous... I like it already. So where do I sign?
Ha-ha. No need for such formalities. They leave a lasting record. I'll meet you in space, Herr Trent. Tschuss!
Jacobo?
Hello. Do I know you?
Wilhelm sent me.
Ah crap.
And what does the esteemed Herr Wilhelm need with me?
Coordinates of a certain informant's shipwreck.

Ah a spy. Yeah I think I know a number of candidate shipwrecks that might fit the bill. I'll even throw in all the locations of all Corsair attacks dating back a month... no make that half a year... Accuracy of twenty millimeters, give or take a couple. No need to thank me.
That won't be necessary, just the potential informer's wrecks. We'll fly together.
And why should I risk my neck? I hate flying.

Well, Wilhelm said that you'd be my guide, and time is money. How would I know you're not bullshitting me and wasting my time putting me on some wild goose chase while you kick up your heels and vanish? The Rheinland military is full of character... well so is this freelancer. You smell me?
A hundred times I curse the day I agreed to help that accursed Wilhelm.
Where is that laggard now? Chilling in some bar? Or beach? Or a bar on a beach?
Well, I know his type. Whatever action happens, we'll be the two in the thick of it while he kicks back and reaps the rewards.
So, the infamous Trent.
My reputation precedes me, Mr... Umm...?
Reichmann. Admiral Reichmann, if you may.
An honour, Admiral Reichmann! What am I so famous for, pray tell?
The inner circles have been all abuzz about the conquering hero in his piece of crap ship. I hope Herr Wilhelm has been compensating you adequately.
No complaints here.
Modesty - a commendable and often underrated virtue, Herr Trent. I'll make sure to double your payment. All the best to your travels, Herr Trent!
So Wilham, you really think that he's the one?
Undoubtedly, Admiral. I can vouch for him personally. He's perfect.
Will you stake your reputation and career on him?
Without hesitation.
Very well, execute your plan.
Yes Sir. Thank you for your trust.
Trust... we shall see. You're dismissed, Herr Wilhelm.
Oh, lookie. A little mouse, scampering into mi casa.
Nah, looks like scrap to me
Recycle 'em, boys.
Don't worry little mousies, it's for the greater good. Recyclingness is Godliness!
Greetings, gentlemen.
Herr Trent, please meet Herr Hassler. This next mission will require both of you to work closely together.
An honor to meet you, Herr Hassler.
And what will we be doing on this mission?
The usual. Hours of boredom, seconds of terror, fly vast distances, blow things up. Nothing special.
While a certain someone is watching safely from afar. Starting to see a pattern here. Could you be any less specific?
Of course. Rhineland intelligence has managed to track down Dietrich's position. He's camping out on an old military base in Konigsberg.
We are amassing a strike fleet to raid his base as we speak. However our analysts project we will suffer massive casualties if we stage a frontal assault on Konigsberg.
That's why we're forming a secondary strike team, which will neutralize the base's defense systems just in time for our main strike fleet to sweep in and decimate it.
Let me guess, you need some stooges to make up the secondary strike team...
You are so good at guessing, Herr Trent. By the way, Admiral Reichmann personally requested for you to be on the secondary strike team.

I don't know whether to be flattered or flustered. Could you explain to me how an ultra-secure military base with best in class defense systems, smack in the center of Rheinland came to be abandoned and fall into the hands of Corsairs, rebels and riff-raff?

During the Kusari wars there were two major bases nearing completion in Rheinland territory - Konigsberg and Regensburg, both were in the Munich system, on the border with Kusari. The Kusari military saw Regensburg as a mere thorn in their side. Konigsberg, however was more significant strategically.

During our last conflict with Kusari, we were dealt a crushing defeat and under the terms of the resulting armistace we were forced to demilitarize Munich. The construction of Konigsberg was halted just before completion...

Our government strangely did not take steps to scuttle or dismantle Konigsberg base. Perhaps they were hoping for a re-negotiation of the peace treaty, or perhaps they had some other scheme lost to history, I don't know. Eventually, Dietrich, having turned coat, and being in possession of all the access keys, just waltzed in and claimed it...
I'm guessing that asking whether I have a choice or not to participate is a stupid question.
You so wise, for a stupid man, Herr Trent.

Herr Trent, ninety percent of the local freelancers could only dream of being in your shoes. Astronomical pay and reporting directly to none other than the legendary Admiral Reichmann. Something others would die for. In fact, many have.
Are you well? You look as nervous as a highschool girl on graduation day. Or prom night. Ha ha. Let's fly. See you in space.

The locals haven't reported anything unusual. Anyway, thank you, Trent. Your work here is done, we'll continue searching for the transport on our own. Unfortunately, since we screwed up, Reichmann cut your payment significantly .
Crap. The rebel base was destroyed, Dietrich's dead, yet Reichmann freaks out and stiffs me because of some puny transport. I'm not a happy camper.
Nor me... The money's been transferred to your account. Go get a drink on me. See you later.
Herr Trent, is that you?
Thank you so much for coming. I need your help. I'm in big trouble. Rheinland authorities are coming for me.
I figured. Rheinland seems to be making a habit of roughing up civilians.

No, Herr Trent, you do not understand. I know too much. They are trying to kill me. Please, I must deliver these documents to Liberty - everything is explained inside. The fate of the universe depends on it.
Yet again I'm dragged into a game of international espionage and subterfuge... Jacobo, are you aware I literally just did a job for the very same Rheinland authorities you're running from now?
Herr Trent, you're a freelancer. You did not take an oath. You owe your allegiance to no one. After a job is done, it is done. I will make it worth your while.
When we deliver these top secret documents to the Forbes system, Liberty will pay us a boat load of money, and I mean a huge aircraft carrier sized boat of money... do you understand?
I know I won't make it without your protection...
If you don't help me, I'm a dead man...
I'm so gonna regret doing this... Sigh. Okay, what's the plan?
Herr Trent, my saviour! I'll make sure to pay off whatever regrets you might have in triplicate! Launch into space. Meet me in orbit.
See you up there, Jacobo.
Gentlemen.
Miss Hatcher.
Why Miss Hatcher, what big eyes you have.
Cut the crap mister, you don't wanna see my teeth. I bite.
Anyway, let's get to business. You two have done a stand-up job.
I won't ask how you managed to escape Rheinland in possession of something like THIS.
I'm afraid it might be too much for my delicate disposition.
*coughs* Well, let's just say we did what we had to do.
Sounds like you two had fun. Good job again. By the way, we're in the market for top Freelancers to execute some... unusual missions. Are you two available?
For you, Miss Wolf, anything...
Shut up, Alaric. Well, seeing as we're now enemies of Rheinland, I suppose some vacancies have opened up.
So, if say I had a couple of well-paying missions...
Say no more. That is, unless these missions wind up turning all of Liberty against us too...
Oh no, I don't think you'll be in that deep.
That's what she said...
Awesome, Trent! Who knew you'd turn out so good at bagging clients and closing deals? The student has become the master!
Seems more like my talent is making enemies and getting us half killed.
Oh come now... one moment you're a newbie freelancer, the next you're raking in big bucks from international governments! Don't sell yourself short!
Mhm, well we're wanted fugitives of one of those government now. Think they'll forget about us anytime soon? I kinda crave Sauerkraut.
Well, word is the Rheinland military has much bigger fish to fry. I doubt they'll bother coming after small fry like us.
Hmm. I know that tone of voice. Same's when you went after my ex girlfriend... Come on, Alaric, what are you hiding from me?
That was a long time ago... and nothing happened. That foxy lady, Miss Hatcher, you don't know who she is?
Yeah sure I do. She's our next paycheck. And way out of your league. Spit it out, Alaric.
She's only one of the most senior officers in one of Liberty's most clandestine agencies.
Oh...
Yeah. It's so secret most of Liberty doesn't even know it exists.
So then how do you know about it, Alaric?
Oh look at the time... I need to go...
I can't believe this is happening again! Just my dumb luck.
This is commander Marcus Creitmire of the Hessian Lions special operations unit.
Power down your weapons immediately and follow our lead. If you resist, we are authorized to use deadly force.
Herr Creitmire, this is Admiral Reichmann. Congratulations on completing your mission.
Take the Dromedary to base for inspection. Dispose of the escort.
Mr. Trent, I see that you're still alive and well.
Well enough Miss Hatcher, I'm not getting any younger, unlike you.
Mr. Trent, flattery will get you nowhere.
Okay then let's skip the niceties and get down to business.
My sentiments exactly.
We've analyzed the documents and they've been very enlightening. However, there's a problem.
Typical. There's always a problem.

They're very esoteric papers containing some extremely complex mathematical equations and high level scientific postulates... but they're light on actual words. Our military scientists can't make head or tail of them. There have been some very heated arguments about whether they describe the end of times, the the start of a glorious new age, plans for a monstrous mecha or even a recipe for a galactic dessert...
You know, watching scientists argue is... almost as exciting as watching paint dry.
So glad to have missed that. So how do I come into the picture? You want me to referee your scientists in their deathmatches? I have a mean left hook...
We need you to recruit the help of a particular scientist who's a key opinion leader in his field. Someone who can shed light on these papers and translate them into lay speak.
His name is Professor Mandrake.
Sounds toxic. And you can't just call him on his pad because...?
He's a recluse, and very, very hard to get hold of. He's currently on a research expedition for the Deep Space Engineering company and completely incommunicado.
So, track down someone who doesn't want to be found and drag him back here kicking and screaming...
Fly to DSE HQ in Detroit station, locate Professor Mandrake, and bring in. Immediately, Mr Trent.
Here's my business card in case DSE's security staff give you any trouble. Tell them you're working for me.
Hmm... Alliance Security Force? ASF? Never heard of it.
Yes. Your reward for completing this assignment will more than generous.
Yes ma'am. That's all I needed to know.
O-kay freelancer, you've got quite a mouth on you, now it's time see if you've got the chops to match. We'll be watching you...
Hey, bro! Got some of the good stuff? Been flying in space so long my ass has gone numb, could really use something to relax...
No way, man! Been doing this shit for hours now. Good stuff doesn't come by easy!
Those assholes from Deep Space Engineering really screwed me over. I did a long haul delivery for them, but the piss-heads won't let me land back on Detroit! Not even for a quick pee break. Ingrates!

Such a shame, I've got some really exotic... stuff in my hold... all the way from Omicron, and now my buyer's pulled the plug 'cos I couldn't land and deliver them personally. Bastard found another seller.
What am I gonna do with all this high quality product... going to... waste. So sad.
Now if only a landing security pass for Detroit could somehow find its way to me... I'd be more than happy to share...
Ooh, friend... What's your name?
Trent. And you are?
Smith. Mister Smith.
Nice to meet you, Mister Smith. You were saying...?
Yeah? Yeah... Oh, yeah! I think I could set you up with a pass.
Oh, really. Tell me more.

I know of a secret warehouse nearby. They might have a spare pass or two there. Guards are my good buddies. Well, you could try walking in the front door yourself, but no telling what they'd do you. If you know what I mean.
Help a friend out, bro?
Come back with that good stuff and we got a deal...
Hey friend, I'm looking for a professor named Mandrake. Heard of him?
Nope.
Aren't you a chatty one. I'm from the bartender's union. Help a brother out?
Oh shit, you're one of those... just show it to the camera over there, and I'll check with our AI system.
Okay got it. He's on a remote research station in Sigma-17.
What kind of station?
Re-se-arch Station. Got it?
OK, man. Thanks for your help. See how nice it is once we melt the ice?
That's what Humanity needs – a little bit more warmth.
Professor Mandrake.
Miss Hatcher.
Professor, I apologize for Tilton delaying you in your capsule over an hour. It must have been uncomfortable.
That bastard, I thought he was over you but he clearly isn't, Miss Hatcher.
Yeah, well the more he tries, the dumber he gets.
You'd better be careful, Miss Hatcher. Statistically, if he tries enough times, he will eventually achieve his goal.
Tilton? Insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results. The fool is incapable of change.
Yeah, but these "progressive ideas" of his about the Order having outlived its usefulness, and Liberty needing to pull the plug on it...
Only fools like him would lend him support, and there aren't many fools like him.
Uh excuse me? I'm right here. Could someone fill me in?
Too difficult and time consuming.
How about we start with the basics, what's the Order?
The Order, Trent is an organization...
I got that much. Please don't patronize me. What do they do? Are they the bad guys or the good guys?
Tell him.
Okay fine. But what I'm about to say is highly classified. If you ever disclose it...
Yeah, yeah, I get it. You'll bite my head off.
Don't flatter yourself. That's Tilton's kind of gig. I prefer performing orchidectomies.
Okay, I'm shaking in my boots. Strictly between us.

Nobody knows how exactly the Order was formed, or who founded it. All we know is that it's been around for a very, very long time, and its' goal is to ensure humanity's survival by monitoring for extinction level threats,
Not trivial things like wars between nations. Not even the 80-year war, which claimed innumerable lives.
The Order only intervenes when humanity faces extinction. One such threat occurred a while back,
when we encountered a parasitic, mind-controlling alien race. That threat was neutralized by the Order.
I remember. There was a number of sudden unexpected deaths among top government officials from different nations. The media described it as a series of unfortunate coincidences.
No coincidence. The media covered it up at the will of their collective governments. Humanity was on the verge of all-out interstellar war, our leaders puppeted by an alien race called the "Nomads".
Disguised as isolated "cross-border incidents".
Exactly. But in reality, these weren't isolated border incidents. It was a war of everyone against everyone, and the Order against the "Nomads".
All those who had a hand in overcoming the Nomads were rewarded discreetly, and the matter was buried.
Oh, Major King, Jun'Ko Zhane and my namesake, Edison Trent?
He's smarter than he looks.
I'm not so sure... Anyway, Trent, the Order coming out of the shadows put it at immediate risk.
In our Liberterian society where democracy is supposedly sacrosanct, the sad truth is whoever rises to the top of the shit pile is king.
And so a horde of rival organizations has appeared, all hell-bent on usurping the Order.

If you sent them into battle against the Nomads they'd shit their pants and run home with their tails between their legs. But right now, after such a long period of peace, these pampered upstarts are happy to politic the Order out of existence in a war of words.
And the Order itself has softened, done in by internal egos and petty conflicts.
...and they lived happily ever after, right?.
Don't interrupt... I'm still talking. The Order fractured into two separate entities: The Alliance Security Force, and the new Order.
The Order is dead? Tell me it ain't so, mummy.
Not quite. Today, the Alliance Security Force oversees Liberty but faces low-level resistance from some of the other Liberterian sub-factions.

The new Order operates out of the shadows, a shadow of its' former self. It supposedly remains true to its' original goal – to protect humanity from extinction level threats. But they rarely make an appearance, dwindling away with time.
I'm so confused...
Now you know, Trent. Run along now, the grown ups need to talk.
Okay.
Professor, Rheinland officials have managed to steal our intel on Omicron Alpha...
And I should care because?
They've set up camp around it and are experimenting on it right now.

What? Are they out of their minds??? The fools!!! Who knows what could happen! Why was't the Sphere secured? Hatcher, how could the Order have allowed this??? Mr. Trent is right... it really is dead...
About Mr. Trent...
Why are you still here?
Spare change?
Ah, yes, of course. I'm transferring you your credits now. We'll be in touch. Professor, I have some Rheinland documents I need you to take a look at...
Hey, what the hell? A visitor!
You! You're not welcome here. Lose something, or looking to lose something?
Not again! Smith, that stupid blabbermouthed junkie… I swear I'm going to end him one of these days.
Let's deal with this moron first. Get him!
Freelancer alpha-one, power down your weapons and follow us to the battleship Griffin.
Freelancer alpha-one, I repeat, power down your weapons and follow us to battleship Griffin. This is a direct order from Commander Tilton. If you fail to comply, we will open fire.
This man is responsible for the destruction of Clark research station! And I have been granted the authority to deal with him as I please!
Shut up, Freelancer!
Attention, we're reading incoming hostiles on radar!
What a pleasant surprise to encounter you here, Herr Trent! Rheinland sends its regards. All wingmen, destroy the freelancer!
Whoa there, boys! Freelancer alpha-one is under my employ. He's on our side. Is that clear?
Shut up, Trent!
Knock knock. Anybody home?
A little bird told me that I could get a Detroit security pass for a reasonable price here.
What the... I'm a freelancer escorting these folks to Forbes, what right do you have...
I'm responsible for WHAT? The station blew up from the inside, while I was waiting outside in space waiting for...
Miss Hatcher. Alaric, I didn't expect to see you here already!
I flew to see Miss Hatcher right away as soon as she contacted me. Looks like I was closer to Norwich than you were.
Gentlemen, now that we're all caught up with our travel itineraries, shall we get down to business?

So, to recap, you both remember the alien artefact we call The Sphere. Originally discovered by The Order, it was one of a very few active, and by far the largest and most complex artefact ever discovered. Naturally, it generated immense... interest amongst the houses. Everyone tried claim a stake in it. However despite the best efforts to crack it, it remained an inscrutable and eventually uncrackable puzzle. Left to rot.

However, thanks to Jacobo's misappropriated documents, we've learnt that the Rheinlanders are on the cusp of figuring out the technology required to to communicate with it, and are currently working on it even as we speak. Based on his readings, Professor Mandrake believes that the Sphere is a shuttered gateway to another system housing hostile beings wielding such unimagineable power even the creators were terrified of them. We need your help to stop the Rhinelanders before they activate the sphere and re-open the portal.

Ha-ha-ha! Perfect. So, if you guys can't work out the Sphere, then no one else can! And if someone else gets to it first, then either the key or The Sphere itself has to go. Bravo! This way no one will ever get in there.

I don't appreciate you sarcasm, Mr. Trent. Remember, it's already happened once, when the other group of Rheinland scientists blundered into the Nomads in Omicron sector... Oh, how I despise these meddlesome Rheinlanders...
It escalated into the crisis we spoke about with Prof. Mandrake. You get the idea, right?
Yeah, I get it. Pandora's Box.
Very well. For this mission you’ll both be receiving triple the usual payout, and elevated to official partners of the ASF.
Hell yeah, I'm in! Where do I sign? I'll sign in blood if needed!
Calm down, Alaric. Miss Hatcher, what exactly is the objective? Destroy The Sphere? Kill the scientists? I can’t just murder on a dime - I'm a lover, not a killer.
Oh, is that so? I had no idea. Professor Mandrake thinks he's worked out a way to render The Sphere inert to external influences.
I'll provide the full details, but only if you accept this mission.
I'm having a de-ja-vu moment. Only last time, I was called "Herr Trent", not "Mr. Trent"... On the other hand, I can't say it was boring. Alright, count us in.
Then I'll meet you both in orbit; we'll continue our conversation there.
Alright, gentlemen, our primary objective is the termination of a Rheinland scientist named Professor Rotterman.
Called it.
“Called it?” … You were hoping for a moonlit walk on the beach?
Grow up, Mr. Trent. Everything is on the line. We must do what needs to be done, morals and ethics be damned.

Your secondary objective is to secure the two alien artifacts crucial for communicating with the Sphere: the Nomad Crystal and the Proteus Tome. They should be in Professor Rotterman's posession, or at least close by.
These artifacts were once kept secure by The Order, but during the "Chaotic" time of the Schism, they were misplaced.
According to Professor Mandrake all we have to do to deactivate the Sphere is to remove the artefacts from its vicinity.
The Order? "Chaotic" times? Schism?
I'll fill you in later, Alaric. It's a lot to take in.
Guys, stop interrupting me! We're wasting time!
Respectfully, Miss Hatcher, Alaric and I are putting our lives on the line. We deserve to know ALL the details - no nasty surprises, especially if you want us to succeed.
Point taken. Ok, firstly, getting inside the complex housing The Sphere isn't going to be easy. It's locked down tight - there's more security swarming over that place than the Kaiser’s palace.
Secondly, there's a massive shipyard set up practically on top of The Sphere; intel indicates two battleships and four mid-sized vessels at the least. A brute force approach isn't going to work.
We're providing you with some prototype cloaking devices the Order has been developing which should turn your ships invisible to radar and vision.
They work by warping the curvature of space around your ships, essentially phasing your ships into a parallel universe for a while.

Installation is simple: hook them up behind your seats, plug the big power cable into your power generator, and run the small control cable to your HUD interface. There's just one on / off button - even you stable geniuses should be able to figure it out.
Press once to cloak. Press again and to decloak.
Be warned that the cloak technology is still unstable, and unfortunately single-use. So after 30 minutes, or after deactivation, you're done for good.
Unstable? Done for good? Does it self destruct or something? Can't we just steal Rheinland cloaking tech?
Where do you think we got the blueprints from. You don't want to know what happens when Rhineland cloaks overheat. Don't worry, ours just melt down a little. You'll be okay.
Before any wisecracks about hot asses, you'll barely feel the heat. The devices have elaborate cooling systems that keep fire risk at a minimum.

If 30 minutes isn't enough, you can opt to maintain the cloak, but at your own risk. Theoretically, if you fail to deactivate the device in time and your ship is still in warped space, you could remain stuck there...
In the other dimension?

We don't know, Alaric. Perhaps you could find out and send us a postcard? Oh, and one last thing: you can't shoot while cloaked. Your projectiles won't be able to escape the bubble of distorted space.
Here is a 3D map of The Sphere from our intelligence agents.
Wow, just look at the size of it...
That's what she said. Great now you've got me doing it. Please upload the data into your computer. You’ll be relaying it, and all updates to Trent throughout the mission.
Lastly, after you arrive in Rheinland, you are to maintain strict radio silence. If you so much as squeak they'll be all over you and the mission will fail before it even gets started.
Okay, that's it. Mount up, gentlemen.
You have a real talent for getting us into sticky situations, Alaric.
What do you mean?
You know.
Are you talking about the mission?
Yeah, SUICIDE mission.
Think of the paycheck!!! 'sides, you could've said "no" at any time.
I was afraid if I said "no", I'd end up flying in space without a spacesuit.
Yeah. Hatcher scares me too. Come on, Trent, let’s just do it. Next time round I’ll let you choose the contract, I promise.
Assuming there’s a "next time". I got a bad feeling about this one.
Trent, we don't have much time. The bomb is already ticking.
Bomb? I thought we were going to deactivate the sphere, not blow it up!
That's plan A. But if Plan A doesn't work out... well now you know Hatcher's fallback plan.
Thanks a lot. Makes me feel all warm and toasty.
Holy crap, look at that...
Trent we need to skedaddle! You can play with it later!!
Trent, we have an emergency! Rheinland gunboats just fired a spread of torpedoes at Missouri.
Our hyperdrive isn't spooled up yet and our defense systems won't be able to handle all the torpedoes.
But don't we need to unload the artifacts first...
Save lives first! Artefacts later!! Get on it!!
Captain Ceed, we've found the artifacts present and intact in the Freelancer's cargo hold.
Excellent work, guys. You bring the artifacts to storage. We'll escort the prisoners to the brig.
At ease, soldier. Head on up to the control room and tell them to issue a transport. We need to deliver these prisoners to base. In the meantime, I'll start interrogating them.
Sir, but what if...
Relax. They're wearing shock collars - they won't dare try anything.
Immediately, sir.
Don't worry, lads, I'm on your side. Count your lucky stars I was on duty.
Forgot to introduce meself. Ceed, Harry Ceed, Order Captain by day. ASF Lieutenant by night. Double agent. Spy extraordinaire.
We're just going to kick our heels up for a while, and when the time is right I'll sneak you off the Nebuchadnezzar.
Do you guys get the feeling this is just another Order trick to get us in the line of hostile fire...
You got a better idea? I dunno about you but I'd rather take my chances getting shot at on the run than being interrogated here by these guys.
Captain, what about the artifacts?
They're being transported to an Order base.
Isn't ASF going to hold you to task for letting that happen?
Got it all covered, along with your escape plan.
Okay, so, what’s our escape plan?
Step one, put these civilian clothes on
Step two, follow me to Mr. Trent’s ship in the hanger. Act natural.
Unfortunately, all your other ships have been stripped for parts already. Luckily, they haven't gotten to Mr Trent's ship yet.
What's step three? How're you getting out of this?
Step three. Rough me up and knock me out. I'll tell them you overpowered me and escaped.
They're not going to divert significant resources to chase down a few escaped prisoners with those precious artefacts in transit.
Clever. Clever spy.

Mr. Trent, I'd like to thank you for all the help. Please accept our apologies for dragging you into such a dangerous situation, and I promise that I'll do everything I can to restore your reputation with Liberty when we can.
Well that's all fine and dandy, but what do I do now?

Keep a low profile. Feel free to work a few jobs here on this freeport, or any other independent stations, or hell, possibly even work for the pirates. But under no circumstances return to lawful space.
If you're caught there, we won't be able to help you. You'll be turned into a scapegoat and executed. Or worse.
I need to contact ASF headquarters right away to discuss the situation and develop an action plan.

As a token of our gratitude, I'm transferring you 5,000 credits from my personal account. Additionally, the promised reward from this mission still stands, and you should receive it as soon as our situation is resolved.
And what about compensation for all the emotional damage?

Mr. Trent, I'm pretty sure whatever emotional damage you had was pre-existing.... Frankly speaking, you've been extraordinarily calm, precise and reliable throughout this entire mission. You strike me as a professional, paid his weight in gold for the quality of his work, and proud of it.
Don't make me think you're a greedy person... greedy people live much shorter lives, in my experience... I'll be in touch once I’ve got news. Stay safe.
ASF intel calls it the 'The Nomad Seed'. It's a gate to a pocket dimension. If the Nomads sense your presence they'll start swarming out of it.
The exit is around here somewhere, but was automatically sealed after the Seed activated. In order to unseal it, you'll need to eliminate all the threats:
The only problem is, if you make too much noise, our Rheinland friends will join the party. So, you have to act quickly. Destroy the Seed first.
This is Delta leader; I'm sending you the coordinates for the Sigma-17 jump hole.
Captain Ceed, targets successfully intercepted.
Immobilize them and deliver them to Nebuchadnezzar.
Alaric, there's some kind of crystal surrounded by a swarm of Nomad ships in here.
Something to drink?
Liberty ale. Got anything for a pro out for big bucks?
Yeah buddy? Look around you... look like there's big bucks here?
In that case... got anything for a dead broke freelancer, will work for peanuts...
Alright, Peanut...
Mr Trent.
Sure. Mr Peanut. I might have something for you if you're up for it.
Some Liberty parasites recently took root in our turf. Shiny new ships, slick dressers. They call themselves Starline Express.
Your task is to take out their leader, Bill Ironside. They're flashy but no pushovers. Interested?
But as discussed, peanuts.
I'll take whatever I can get. Send me the brief.
Hey, bro, know where Rockford's at?
None of your bees wax.
Tough guy, eh, shithead? Best answer before we make you.
This'll make you talk.
Where's Rockford, you prick?
I'm right here.
Follow me. Immediately!
Dammit Rockford, I'm immobilized!
Dammit Rockford, I'm immobilized!
I know.
Rockford, what's going on? You told me you're ASF!
Rockford, what's going on? You told me you're ASF!
How guillible you are, Mr Trent.
If I go down, I'm taking the artefacts with me!
If I go down, I'm taking the artefacts with me!
Apologies. The artefacts are nigh indestructible. They will survive the explosion of your ship.
Ah crap. Come on you old rust-bucket. Don't fail me now!
I need help! It's a matter of national security!
Oh really? If so, then you should seek advice from a representative of the State.
Officer Darcy is a Representative of Bretonia. Best there is.
Hi, Officer Darcy. My name is Trent. I'm working for a secret organisation called the Order, and I need to contact them ASAP.
Another loser... Sir, you must know that smuggling alien artifacts is illegal...
We caught a pair of your buddies recently. Claiming to be Order agents too, locked 'em up good.
Guess you'll be wanting to join them... or perhaps, that other guy, Napoleon in the mental asylum.
Look I'm not kidding. I need to deliver some artefacts of utmost importance to Order HQ as soon as possible.
Or else I'll be executed, and anyone who's associated with me... that includes you. Look just take a look okay?
Oh, wow... this is... different.
How am I supposed to know this isn't just some souvenir from a gift-shop?
Goddamn it... I'm telling you...
Okay don't get your knickers in a twist. I have a friend who collects and deals in antiquities and curiosities.
Let's go visit him and have him validate this. If he does, I'll help you in any way I can.
But if it's a fake... Napolean could do with some company. He's partial to handsome young men.
Err. Okay. By the way, I have a small problem with my ship... It's pretty much fried. It's a miracle I made it here at all.
All right, i'll let you use one of ours, for a small fee.
But if you decide to run off with it... think twice. It's a military ship so its' equipped with a tracker. You can run, but you can't hide.
Wow, talk about eclectic tastes.
Rare trinkets generate huge profits from buyers with unusual tastes, Mr Linguist.
Ms Darcy. You look well.
Hi, Jabba. I need you to check out something for me.
Hmm. Yes.. this... is evidently of alien origin.
I'll pay you ten thosands credits for it right now, Mr Linguist.
Oh... wow... So much for the Barman's "fake as fake can be, drinks on me". Okay, Trent, we're outta here.
Jabba, Not a peep to anyone, you got it?
Of course, Ms Darcy, of course...
Thanks Trent. While one good turn deserves another, your side-quest will have to wait. Turns out that jerk wasn't always "buying" his stuff... if you get what I mean.
And those goons of his who attacked us earlier are wanted for murder too. Paperwork... my old enemy.
Oh yes before I forget, payment for your troubles, from the Bretonian goverment. Ten thousands credits.
Gonna take more than that to make me part with the artefact, Darcy.
Yeah-yeah. Very funny, Trent. See you later.
See you sooner, Darcy.
Freelancer, you've got something we want. Hand it over!
Boys, have you completely lost your minds? This is my turf, I'm top dog around here. Trent, let's wipe the floor with these scum.
Trent. Behind that door are some really really big names. I'm talking huge.
Please try to behave with some restraint.
Dont know what you're talking about. I'm always on my best behaviour. Paragon of restraint, me.
Ah, Ms.Darcy - our beauty with brains, and hope for a brighter age.
And this must the Freelancer. I've heard so much about you.
Yes, this is Mister Trent. Trent, this are Admiral Brighton, and the honorable Princess Caitlin.
We have a matter of the utmost importance to discuss with you, mister Trent.
Really? Not again.
Mr.Trent, please try not to be flippant. This matter is of fundamental importance to Bretonia.
Trying my best.
We have a mission that requires to your very specific skillset.
My specific skillset?
Order, Mr.Trent, Order.
A burger and...
Mr.Trent, I must inform you that this mission is being overseen by the very highest ranking officials of Bretonia.

That her royal highness is in attendance should inform even someone like you of the gravity of this matter, and perhaps hint at the bare modicum of decorum necessitated. We would most appreciate it if you could take this just a little seriously.
Beware of masters, they / Will cause you trouble any day. / Of all the woes may God deliver us from both. / From their love and their wrath.
We also fail to appreciate your skepticism, and what you appear to believe is humour, Mr.Trent.
We would ask a favour of you, and in return we offer an opportunity.
Okay. Fine. What is the nature of this favour?
Much better, Mr.Trent. Milady, may I?
Please...
Mr.Trent, quite a while ago the government of Bretonnia entered into an agreement with the Order.
It boiled down to the fact that Bretonia... well...
Mr.Trent, have you heard of the Nomad problem?
Yep.
Excellent. A little caution can't hurt, if you know what I mean.
Under this agreement, Bretonnia renounced its interests in the sectors of the so-called "The Nomad Legacy". that is, the nomads. Are you following, Mr. Trent?
Yep.
Hmm, fine. In exchange, the Order agreed to prohibit access to these systems to all parties. Completely.
In our naivete, we assumed that ASF would adhere to the agreement, as the progeny of the Order. But now...
Now... What?...
They are permitting the bastards from the IRA to colonise Tau-44, and at a prodigious speed.
How horrific. What's the IRA by the way?
Not "what" but "who". They're a group of political, idealogical and religious fanatics, demanding independence for Ireland from the Crown of Bretonia.
That's rich, given that there're neither Ireland nor a true monarchy in Sirius sector. Bretonia is a constitutional monarchy.
Mr.Trent...
What? As far as I know, there's no planet or station called Ireland.
But there are still Irish people, unfortunately...
Do you realize now how ridiculous this is, Mr.Trent?
So what do you want me to do?
Fly to Tau-44 and purge it of all IRA presence.
We also suspect that the ASF is tied up with all of this. And that's where you come in.
Me? How? As someone who points his finger at someone else and says, "He's from the ASF"? That doesn't sound too convincing to me.
Uhhh...
Does fifty thousand credits sound convincing? Just to go for a little walk in the park.
A walk in the park? For fifty thousand? Maybe I was too quick to say that there is no Bretonian Crown in Sirius sector.
Cleverer than he looks. Admiral Brighton will have direct oversight of this operation, please discuss all the details with him.
That will be all...
Trent, my battleship, the Prince of Wales, is orbiting the planet. Dock on it, and I'll transfer all the necessary passes and permits to you.
Well Trent, see you on the "Prince of Wales".
Trent, get your ship ready, we've almost reached the launch point.
What, no briefing at all?
We're getting conflicting data from Tau-44. We'll have to play it by ear.
So we're improvising?
Exactly.
Majo... uhhm... Sorry, General King, Trent has been delivered.
Thank you, Miss Hatcher.
Mr.Trent, I know, it's been a wild ... ahem... couple of days for you...
Weeks...
Even were it months, there are some things take precedence over our mental and physical states. Right now, it is absolutely crucial to determine the location of the Proteus Tome and the Key.
So, please recount to me in detail everything that's happened to you from the moment Miss Hatcher ordered you to fly to Sigma-19 with Delta Squad till this moment. Spare no details.
We were intercepted in Omicron Major, didn't make it to Sigma-19.
Who intercepted you?
Military types from a battleship named the "Nebuchadnezzar". Order I think. A certain Captain Ceed helped us escape...
Captain Ceed...
Ceed...
After that, agent Rockford contacted me. Or rather I contacted him...
Rockford? Rockford who?
Just Rockford. He helped me retrieve the artifacts. But it turned out he wanted them for himself. He turned on me and tried to murder me.
I managed to escape by the skin of my teeth, with the Proteus tome.
So this Rockford person knows...
And he's in the game
We have to fix this.
At the moment he's lurking around in the New Order. We need someone on the inside to help us track him down.
Will you provide us this elusive someone?
No way Jose. I've only got a few assets left within the Order that haven't been compromised.
Perhaps... Mr.Trent could be of assistance?

You're kidding me. Trent? The same Trent that's misplaced two crucial artifacts, squandered an entire cover squadron, earned himself wanted status in Liberty AND Rhineland... you want HIM to infiltrate the Order? He won't last a day! General King, are you out of your mind???
Yeah incompetence to this extent can't be natural. He's probably a double agent for the Order...
My gut tells me to trust him. Trent, help us do this and we'll wipe your record and pay you triple the going rate.
You know what? No dice. Lately it feels like all I'm ever trying to do is patch up my steadily worsening reputation for some measely bucks.
But it keeps ending up with me being hunted down by entire governments and framed for treason. It's like Groundhog Day.
General King, could you remind us of the name of the previous agent we entrusted with infiltrating the Order?
What does it matter? He's offline, almost certainly dead.
General, I suspect Trent will want to hear this.
Alaric. I think, Alaric.
You bastards! What happened to Alaric?
We lost contact with him somewhere in Kusari teritory.
He was supposed to come in from the cold to us after going deep undercover but never made it. We don't know who got their hands on him and whatever information he was carrying.
Trent, how about this. Kill two birds with one stone. Help us, and find your friend at the same time. Retrieve the data your friend was supposed to transfer to us and you both free to go.
And don't even think about doing anything heroic, just don't think. Period.
Yeah, I can do that.
Miss Hatcher, retrieve all data on Agent Alaric and transfer it to mister Trent, please.
Next, your orders are to deliver the Proteus Tome along with Trent and Miss Darcy here to the research base.
Yes Sir!
Glad to see you again, Mr. Trent.
It's good that you managed to deliver at least the Proteus tome to us. Now it will definitely be safe.
At your service, Professor. I'm glad to see you too.
By the way, Mr. Trent, did the Order have any other artifacts?
Well, there was some crystal that I broke. After that, I found myself on the other end of Sirius, in Bretonia.
Ah, so that's how it works!
Is something wrong, Professor?
We ran several experiments, and that artifact simply evaporated. We tried it on people. And they evaporated along with the artifact...
You were lucky to end up in an inhabited system, rather than in empty space a thousand light-years from civilized systems.
So I'm a very lucky guy. You could even say I was born under a lucky star twice over.
Damn, Trent, you really escaped by a miracle.
What's next with the Order, Hatcher?
Nothing yet, I'll keep asking around. I'll let you know when everything is ready. Meanwhile, have fun. I'll give you a small compensation for emotional distress.
And what about the promised two hundred and fifty thousand?
We'll see how you manage to get the second artifact from Rockford. If everything goes well, I promise you an extra bonus on top.
Promises again... And where will that lead everyone...
Alright, take care. I'll get to some real work. Waiting for your call.
Mission parameters have been adjusted. We're receiving new intelligence. Hold please.
The IRA base in Tau-44 has been destroyed, and there is reason to believe that a... surprise has been left for us in the debris.
Given the circumstances, you and Darcy, operating as private contractors, are to proceed to the sector and investigate with utmost caution.
Trent??? You??? What are you doing here? And in company of a Bretonian operative!
Don't make any sudden moves or my boys will grind you and your Bretonian girlfriend to dust.
Yes, silence, bitch. Now is my time. Captain Warfish, are the cruiser's batteries ready?
Capacitors charged to forty-three percent.
We have a couple of minutes then. What is "here"? "Here" is the Nomad's Lair. What are we doing here? Doing God's work. Executing our government's orders. Taking control.
The Order betrayed us. Liberty supported The Order in its infancy without constraint, without reservation... but after The Order gained power, it failed to reciprocate.

All data on Nomad technology was seized and removed from circulation by the Order's top brass. All that opportunity to leap ahead of the other governments, squandered. The Schism bought us enough disarray and confusion for our agents of ASF to appropriate information related to this place.
The Nomad's Lair is a massive crucible for the sole purpose of forging Nomad fighters. If we activate it, Liberty will be invincible! Unlimited Nomad Pods at our disposal! My brain trembles!
Each pod, unfurling into a swarm of fighters... the spear of destiny, raining hellfire unto our heathen enemies!
Sir, capacitors are fully charged.
And you, Lady and not so Gentleman, have the honor of witnessing this historic moment for Liberty, for posterity!
Silence, curs. Captain Warfish, fire at will.
Uh... Commander Tilton, are you quite certain? Perhaps we should...
Yes! Goddammit! If you don't fire right now, Warfish, I'll have you court martialled!
Copy that.
Yes, ma'am!
Attention, unidentified vessels! This is...
Bretonian girlfriend? Who the hell do you think...
You're insane!
Trent, Brighton was the only... The only man... The only decent man among all the...
What you need to do is freeze. Don't even breathe.
Mister Trent. You haven't forgotten me, I hope?
You're a real piece of work, Trent. Red Leader, keep your sights trained on this scoundrel. If he so much as twitches a muscle, you are weapons-free. You read?
So, what exactly happened here? And Trent, tell me why it is every time that shit hits the fan you show up like a bad penny? Are you a shit-magnet? A shit-stirrer? JUST WHO THE HELL ARE YOU?!

Perhaps it'd be best if I explain. One of your men — Commander Tilton — attempted to activate this monstrous Nomad facility. Ostensibly it was going to churn out a ceaseless supply of Nomad fighters to quote unquote rain hellfire upon the heathen enemies. Classic small man syndrome.

Frankly, he seemed quite mad, manic, or both. Since he clearly had no idea what he was doing, the facility overloaded. The resulting catastrophic chain-reaction culminated in a massive explosion which obliterated him, his ships, and his men. And a Bretonian battleship, the Prince of Wales, captained by a friend of mine.
Tilton... That megalomaniac... he finally went too far. Sigh. On behalf of Liberty, please accept my condolences for your loss. My thoughts and prayers are with you.

Okay. Now that that's done. You two follow me to base to debrief. Red Leader, stay here and start a preliminary survey of the debris. I'll despatch some eggheads from base later for the scientific survey.
Who are these guys? Since when does Liberty operate out here?
Tilton. Why are YOU here? And what and where exactly is "here"?
Darcy, not now.
Tilton, You don't know what it'll do! It's alien tech! Are you sure it's going to do what you think? What if the Nomad fighters can't be controlled?
I know, Darcy, I know. Look, we need to...
Hatcher, is that you?
Miss Hatcher, I could never forget you even if I tried.
Trent, ready for action?
Yeah. Sure. Uhh... what action was that again, exactly?
We're meeting informants from the Order! We have no idea how many of them there'll be, much less their disposition!
Aren't YOU all the protection I need? Or is Bretonia's influence in Kusari territory dwindling?
Bretonia's influence is doing just fine. But even the strongest political influence can't stop a laser bolt to the head. So play nice.
As you wish, Buttercup.
I'll be honest, it's kind of unsettling how everyone in the bar, including the bartender, is staring at me.
I was going to make a quip about you and main character syndrome, but in this instance I'm inclined to agree with you. They're not sparing me a second glance, which is peculiar.
Yeah. Creepy. If this guy doesn't show in the next thirty minutes, I'm outta here.
I'm with you.
Herr Trent, we meet again.
Herr Hassler? You're the contact? Looking sharp! Out of uniform today?
My service for Rheinland is permanently terminated, Herr Trent. You have witnessed the sunset of a decorated military career. Kaputt. Now I have found a new home with the Order.
But enough about me. Around here, you are a superstar. As you are aware, there is a substantial bounty on your head...
There is? ... Why?

And he doesn't even know. Ha-ha. People are saying that you are one cool cucumber to show up here... if they only knew it was just, how do you say it... ignorance is bliss. Herr Trent, let's just say that you have crossed the Order so many times...our leadership don't just have nervous tics when your name comes up — they have full-blown seizures. And when they recover, they have another seizure...

You seem to attract calamity, yet each time you somehow emerge from the brink of disaster not only unscathed,but with a beautiful girl on your arm, set against the backdrop of a big, black mushroom cloud.
Oh so that's why everyone's gawking at me.
You are a legend. To just waltz into an Order base after all this just to meet me... you are either very brave, or very stupid.Nonetheless, for now you are perfectly safe, as promised.
Hassler, right now I just need answers. I really need to know, where is Alaric? Is he alive and well?
For this, Herr Trent, you will have to speak to the head of the New Order, Herr Yamamoto.
Can you set it up?
Already on it!
Let's not be too hasty...

You're already in New Order HQ. It's a little late to be getting cold feet. Heads up. Yamamoto-san holds deeply conservative views and has a profound respect for martial prowess. Or rather, he only respects martial prowess.

I told him about our previous adventures... or misadventures, and he seems to have developed a peculiar respect for you. Or perhaps a morbid curiosity. Or both. I don't believe you're in any danger. Not mortal danger at least.
Into the Dragon's maw!
Herr Yamamoto please meet Herr Trent and Fraulein Darcy.
Mr. Trent, I thought that at my age I had lost all capacity for surprise, but you, you surprise me. One could write an epic tale about your adventures. Or two!

One day you are a nobody, the next day you work for the intelligence service of one state, then you become an enemy of that state, and then suddenly you are working for the intelligence service of another, and then you are most wanted by THAT state! Ha ha. It is very entertaining.
And then you casually cast the long-term plans of a supra-governmental secret organization into the trash. And here you stand, looking surprisingly alive and well, before its leader.
Some sake, Mr. Trent? Miss Darcy?
Thank you, Yamamoto-san.
Thank you, Mr. Yamamoto. I need a favour from you.
Of course, why would you be here otherwise.
I need to locate an Atticus Rockford.
And why is that?
I have a personal score to settle with him.
General King too, it would seem.
Do not be coy, Mr. Trent. I am not some bartender with loose lips.
Besides, I have a feeling King may not feel too kindly about you either...
considering he sent you on a suicide mission...
Suicide mission?!
One man is not enough to eliminate a man such as Rockford. Not even a man as ridiculously lucky as you, Mr. Trent.

I don't give a damn about King's feelings right now, Mr. Yamamoto, or should I say, Yamamoto-san? I'm going track down that murderous bastard Rockford, reclaim what he stole from me and pay him back in kind.
Ah, to be young and passionate again... or foolish...
I will help you, Mr Trent. Rockford is, as you say, "a bone in the throat" for us as well, correct?
But if you want my help, you must return the favour.
I'm not sure we say bone in the throat... sounds kinda dirty. How exactly will I be repaying the favour?
We just need you to deploy an experimental scanner in space. We call it the Chrysanthemum.
Huh, doesn't sound too difficult... What's the catch?

We have interests in the Enterprise system. And knowledge of all defensive measures the ASF has implemented since the schism of the Order. We have the technical means to acquire all the information we need with this scanner.
We just need to deploy it within the Sirius system, which is patrolled by...
The ASF...
So, Mr. Trent, do you agree?
Yeah, why not. Just another day in my life.
In that case, you may depart now. Lieutenant Kim will contact you. He will oversee the operation.
Trent, are crazy? This operation is against the bloody ASF!
Well, Darcy, it's starting to feel like the big Scriptwriter in the Sky is yanking my chain... friend one day, foe the next.
The operation was a complete fiasco!
Kim, stand down please.
You better hold up your end of the deal, or the sacrifices of my men would have been in vain.
We will. I promise
Hey, Hassler, is everyone around here loony-tunes or what?
Not everyone, Herr Trent. But their determination is ...inspiring.
There's another word for it. Anway, what now?
For now, you rest. We have prepared quarters for you and Fraulein Darcy on our battleship. An escort will lead you there.
Matome.. we will honour your memory. Thank you.
Go now! May we meet again, in another life, my friend.
